text:
Sara: heads up — after the kernel-selector roll earlier today I'm seeing a 7-12% p50 increase on host-side latency for streaming requests. writev counts per request spiked.
Raj: do we have a flame/trace for that window?
Sara: uploading flame but quick summary: syscall writev calls x3 vs baseline, small writes dominate. link: https://internal.prod/flames/8012345678 (uploaded)
Evan: confirmed from the trace. gRPC layer is sending lots of tiny frames, TCP_NODELAY behavior changed somewhere. writev count went from ~220 -> ~640 per minute on a single host.
Mike: kernel-selector change moved some requests onto the "fused" attention kernel path — could be changing token chunking alignment earlier in the pipeline.
Sara: also saw KV cache miss rate +15% in same period, which increases token path work. suspect preparse fragmentation now cutting across token boundaries.
Linda: paste of perf top from one host (trimmed):
```
SYSCALL        COUNT
writev         12345
sendto          120
read             90
recvmsg          30
accept            2
```
and a short netstat snapshot:
```
Tcp:   RcvRtt  1ms  Retrans 3  Unacked 0  SndBuf  12KB  RecvBuf 64KB
```
Raj: quick mitigation options: 1) raise write coalesce threshold in the proxy/sidecar (aggregate until >=4KB) 2) toggle SO_SNDBUF/SO_SNDTIMEO knobs 3) short rollback of kernel-selector flag
Evan: I ran a microbench locally. numbers (streaming chat qps=500):
- baseline (pre-roll): p50=28.1ms p95=86ms
- regressed: p50=31.0ms p95=103ms
- proxy-coalesce 4KB: p50=28.4ms p95=88ms
So coalesce threshold gets us basically back to baseline for p50.
Mike: good. I'll prototype a sidecar aggregator that accumulates small frames until threshold or end-of-chunk then writev once. Will add a metric for small-write-rate.
Sara: repro steps I used (streaming):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"x","stream":true,"max_tokens":200}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/generate
```
Observe many sub-100B frames in the trace.
Linda: also need to tweak batch heuristics tests — add synthetic token-length distribution where tokens are skewed to single-char tokens (e.g., code-heavy prompts).
Raj: longer-term: kernel-selector should not alter the ingress fragmentation semantics. Mike/ryan should ensure tokenizer/preparse outputs are invariant across kernel choices (or add explicit re-chunking step).
Mike: will open PR for sidecar coalescing + unit tests. Planning canary on 5 hosts after code review.
Sara: creating issue: INF-1234 with logs, flame, perf numbers, and action items. assigned Mike/ Raj/ Evan. I'll add Linda for test updates.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary-57 -> prod-us-west (rolling 5 hosts).
Evan: after canary started I re-ran the microbench against canary IPs — small-write-rate dropped ~78% and p50 returned to 28.6ms. p95 still slightly high, investigating KV miss side.
Linda: created test case in perf harness: token_lengths=[1,1,1,6,1,1,12] to exercise fragmentation.
Sara: summary/action items:
- Mike: PR for sidecar write coalesce (4KB default) + metrics — due EOD
- Raj: prepare kernel-selector toggle/rollback plan if canary shows regressions
- Evan: dig into KV cache evictions correlated with fragmentation, add telemetry
- Linda: update batch-heuristic unit tests and perf harness
:thumbsup:
Mike: sounds good — starting branch now.
Sara: thanks all, will watch canary and report back in this thread.
